ranked.mechanism: The intermittent stall in shadow is caused by grease solidification in the bearing, which increases static friction (stiction) above the reaction wheel's holding torque, preventing rotation.
ranked.intervention: Introduce a dedicated low-power heating element within the bearing housing to maintain the grease above its solidification threshold.

ranked.mechanism: Cold-temperature exposure causes baseline grease to exceed its critical solidification temperature, drastically increasing shear modulus and causing static friction (stiction) spikes; this prevents the bearing rollers from rolling, leading to stall when torques are low during shadow phase.
ranked.intervention: Replace standard aerospace grease with a specialized low-temperature polyalphaolefin (PAO) grease formulated with high-viscosity-index additives to maintain fluidity down to -65°C, reducing the coefficient of static friction.
